name: ChatGPT
description: An AI assistant for writing, explanations, research, coding and everyday questions.
fullDescription: Chat with an AI assistant, work through questions, draft and revise text, analyze uploaded material, and use supported tools. A free plan is available with usage limits; paid plans add higher limits and more capabilities.
features: File and image analysis on supported plans
Web search and other tools with plan limits
limitations: Free-plan access and tool limits apply and can change
Responses can be inaccurate; verify important information

name: Claude
description: An AI assistant for writing, analysis, coding and working with long documents.
fullDescription: Claude can help explain concepts, draft and edit writing, analyze documents, and assist with software development. Anthropic offers a free plan with limited usage and paid plans with higher capacity.
features: Projects and additional tools on eligible plans
limitations: Free usage is limited and may vary
AI output needs human review

name: Gemini
description: Google’s AI assistant for questions, writing, learning and supported Google services.
fullDescription: Gemini provides conversational AI help for research, writing, explanations and creative tasks. Google offers access without a paid AI plan, while paid Google AI plans increase usage and unlock additional capabilities.
features: Image and file-related capabilities where available
limitations: Features and limits vary by country, account and plan
Some advanced features require a paid Google AI plan

name: Perplexity
description: An AI-powered search and answer engine that provides linked sources.
fullDescription: Ask questions and receive synthesized answers with citations to web sources. The free tier supports basic search and answers; paid plans provide higher limits and additional research features.
limitations: Citations should still be opened and checked
Advanced models and higher usage require paid plans

name: NotebookLM
description: A research assistant that answers questions using the sources you provide.
fullDescription: Upload or add supported sources such as documents, websites and videos, then ask questions grounded in that collection. NotebookLM can help summarize material and create study-oriented outputs. Standard access is available free, with higher limits on eligible paid plans.
features: Audio overviews and other generated formats
limitations: Source and usage limits apply
Generated summaries can omit context or make mistakes

name: Hugging Face
description: Explore, share and build with open machine-learning models, datasets and interactive AI applications.
fullDescription: Hugging Face Hub is a collaborative platform for discovering and sharing machine-learning models, datasets and Spaces (interactive demos). It supports model and dataset repositories, version history and integrations with popular ML libraries. Some hosted compute and advanced features have usage limits or paid options.
features: Browse datasets for AI and research
limitations: Model licences and usage terms vary by repository
Some hosted compute and advanced features have limits or paid plans
Review model cards, dataset documentation and safety information before use

name: Ollama
description: Run supported open AI models locally on your own computer.
fullDescription: Download Ollama to run compatible language models locally, manage models from a command line, and connect local models to supported applications. Local model use does not require a subscription, while optional cloud model services have separate usage and pricing.
features: No subscription required for local inference
limitations: Model downloads can use substantial disk space and RAM
Speed depends heavily on the computer and model size
Optional cloud services are separate

name: GitHub
description: Host code repositories, track changes and collaborate on software projects.
fullDescription: GitHub provides Git-based source control, issue tracking, pull requests and project collaboration. Its Free plan includes unlimited public and private repositories, with additional collaboration and enterprise features on paid plans.
limitations: Some advanced security and organization features require paid plans
Public repositories are visible to everyone

name: Visual Studio Code
description: A free code editor with extensions, debugging and Git integration.
fullDescription: Visual Studio Code is a lightweight source-code editor that supports many programming languages through extensions. It includes editing, debugging, terminal and source-control features and is available for Windows, macOS and Linux.
limitations: Some advanced workflows require extensions or external tools
The editor is not a full IDE for every language

name: MDN Web Docs
description: Reliable documentation and guides for HTML, CSS, JavaScript and web APIs.
fullDescription: MDN is a reference and learning resource for web technologies. Use it to understand browser APIs, language features, HTML elements, CSS properties and practical web-development concepts. Its documentation is freely accessible.
features: Reference documentation for web standards and APIs
limitations: It is documentation rather than a hosted coding environment
Some topics require prior programming knowledge

name: CodePen
description: Write HTML, CSS and JavaScript in the browser and see a live preview.
fullDescription: CodePen is an online code playground for building and sharing small front-end experiments. The free plan includes public Pens and a limited number of files per Pen; privacy and advanced features are part of paid plans.
features: Separate HTML, CSS and JavaScript editors
Public code examples and community projects
limitations: Free Pens are public
The free plan limits files per Pen and has other restrictions

name: StackBlitz
description: Create and run web-development projects directly in your browser.
fullDescription: StackBlitz provides browser-based development environments for web projects, with live previews and project templates. It offers free access with usage and project limits; paid plans provide higher limits and additional features.
features: Run supported web projects in the browser
limitations: Free usage and project limits apply
Large projects may need more resources than a browser can provide

name: Vercel
description: Deploy websites and front-end projects with previews and hosting tools.
fullDescription: Vercel is a deployment platform commonly used for front-end frameworks and web applications. Its Hobby plan is free for personal projects and includes Git-based deployments, previews and a set of usage allowances; other use cases may require paid plans.
features: Free Hobby plan for personal projects
limitations: Hobby plan is intended for personal, non-commercial use
Usage limits and plan terms apply

name: Netlify
description: Build and deploy websites with Git-based workflows and preview links.
fullDescription: Netlify hosts websites and web applications and can connect to Git repositories for automatic builds and deployments. A free plan is available with monthly usage credits and limits; paid plans add capacity and collaboration features.
features: Custom domains with SSL on the free plan
limitations: The free plan has monthly credit and usage limits
Some team and advanced features require paid plans

name: PortSwigger Web Security Academy
description: Free interactive lessons and labs for learning web application security.
fullDescription: PortSwigger's Web Security Academy teaches web vulnerabilities through explanations and hands-on labs. It is designed for legal, controlled practice and covers topics such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting and access control.
limitations: Some exercises require familiarity with HTTP and web applications
Use labs only within their intended environment

name: TryHackMe
description: Guided cybersecurity rooms and browser-based practice for different skill levels.
fullDescription: TryHackMe provides guided cybersecurity learning rooms and practical exercises. It has a free tier with hundreds of rooms and limited AttackBox time; paid plans unlock additional paths, labs and usage.
features: Some free rooms and daily AttackBox access
limitations: Many learning paths and advanced features require a paid plan
Practice only in authorised rooms and environments

name: OverTheWire
description: Learn Linux and security concepts through progressive terminal-based wargames.
fullDescription: OverTheWire hosts community wargames that teach security concepts through practical challenges. Bandit is designed for beginners and introduces command-line and Linux fundamentals. The games are freely accessible.
features: Bandit introduces Unix and Linux basics
limitations: Requires a terminal and basic command-line use
Hints are not always provided; challenges require independent problem-solving

name: picoCTF
description: A cybersecurity learning platform with beginner-friendly capture-the-flag challenges.
fullDescription: picoCTF is an educational CTF platform created by Carnegie Mellon University's CyLab. Learners solve challenges involving areas such as cryptography, web exploitation, forensics and general security in a safe practice environment.
limitations: Some challenges require programming or command-line skills
Only use the platform's authorised challenge environment

name: OWASP Juice Shop
description: An intentionally vulnerable web app for practising web security in a legal lab.
fullDescription: OWASP Juice Shop is an open-source training application containing deliberately introduced security flaws. It is useful for security education, demonstrations and testing defensive tools when run in a controlled environment.
features: Hands-on challenges based on common web vulnerabilities
Can be run locally or in supported training environments
limitations: Intentionally vulnerable; do not expose an unsafe instance to the public internet
Requires setup if run locally

name: CyberChef
description: A browser-based toolkit for encoding, decoding, encryption and data analysis tasks.
fullDescription: CyberChef is an open-source web application developed by GCHQ. It provides a visual recipe-based interface for common data transformations, encoding and decoding, compression, hashing and analysis. Processing is performed in the browser.
features: Large collection of data transformation operations
limitations: It is a utility, not a substitute for understanding cryptography
Use trusted input data and verify important results

name: Khan Academy
description: Free lessons and practice for maths, science, computing and more.
fullDescription: Khan Academy offers structured lessons, practice exercises and instructional videos across school and introductory college subjects. Learners can use it at no cost, while some optional partner or programme features may vary.
limitations: Course coverage and curriculum alignment vary by subject and region
It does not replace a teacher or formal qualification

name: freeCodeCamp
description: Learn programming with free lessons, coding exercises and projects.
fullDescription: freeCodeCamp teaches web development and programming through an interactive curriculum, practice projects and articles. Its learning platform code is open source, while curriculum content has separate copyright terms. The core learning experience is free.
features: Free certifications for completing curriculum requirements
limitations: Self-paced learning requires consistency
Certificates are not the same as an accredited college qualification

name: MIT OpenCourseWare
description: Free course materials from MIT, including notes, assignments and lecture videos.
fullDescription: MIT OpenCourseWare publishes materials from thousands of MIT courses for independent study. Content can include syllabi, lecture notes, readings, assignments and videos. It is free to access and does not provide course credit or certificates.
features: Materials from a wide range of MIT subjects
Lecture notes, assignments and selected videos
limitations: No grades, instructor interaction, academic credit or certificates
Some courses have incomplete or older materials

name: CS50x
description: Harvard’s introductory computer science course, available online for self-study.
fullDescription: CS50x introduces computer science and programming through lectures, problem sets and a final project. Anyone can follow the course online for free. The course describes separate free CS50 certificates and paid verified certificate options through edX.
features: Structured weekly lectures and problem sets
Free self-study route and CS50 certificate subject to completion
limitations: The course is challenging for beginners and requires sustained effort
Verified edX certificates and academic credit are separate and may cost money

name: W3Schools
description: Quick tutorials and examples for web development and programming languages.
fullDescription: W3Schools provides tutorials, references and editable examples for HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, SQL and other technologies. Core tutorials are available free without signing up; premium features and certificates are paid.
features: Examples that can be edited in the browser
limitations: Some practice, progress and certificate features require a paid plan
For deeper topics, compare explanations with official documentation

name: Desmos Graphing Calculator
description: Plot equations, explore functions and visualise maths in an interactive graph.
fullDescription: The Desmos Graphing Calculator lets you graph equations, plot points, explore functions and create mathematical visualisations in a browser. The calculator is free to use, with additional classroom products and services available separately.
limitations: Advanced classroom features are separate from the basic calculator
It is a learning aid, not a replacement for showing working

name: Radio Garden
description: Explore a globe and listen to live radio stations around the world.
fullDescription: Radio Garden lets listeners browse a globe of radio stations and tune in to live broadcasts from different places. Availability and playback depend on each station and regional rights.
features: Discover music and broadcasts from other regions
limitations: Individual stations may be offline or geographically restricted
Station content and advertising are controlled by broadcasters

name: Internet Archive
description: Explore a digital library of books, films, audio, websites and archived material.
fullDescription: The Internet Archive is a non-profit digital library that preserves and provides access to a broad collection of digital materials, including archived web pages, books, audio and video. Access and borrowing conditions vary by item.
features: Browse digitised books, audio and video
Use the Wayback Machine to view archived websites
limitations: Not every item is available for immediate download or streaming
Borrowing and access restrictions vary by item and rights

name: Project Gutenberg
description: Read thousands of free ebooks, especially older public-domain literature.
fullDescription: Project Gutenberg is a volunteer-run digital library offering more than 75,000 free ebooks. Many works are public domain in the United States; users outside the US should check local copyright rules before downloading or redistributing a title.
features: Read online or download in common ebook formats
No registration required for most titles
limitations: Copyright status can differ by country
The catalogue focuses heavily on older works

name: Neal.fun
description: A collection of playful interactive experiments and small web experiences.
fullDescription: Neal.fun hosts creative browser-based projects, visual experiments and interactive experiences made by independent creator Neal Agarwal. It is a lightweight place to explore unusual ideas and short interactive activities.
features: A variety of small interactive projects
Quick experiences that work in a browser
limitations: Individual experiments vary in quality and may change over time
Some experiences may not be suitable for every device or browser

name: itch.io
description: Discover independent games and creative projects, including many free titles.
fullDescription: itch.io is an open marketplace focused on independent games and digital creations. Creators choose how to distribute their work, so the catalogue includes free, paid and pay-what-you-want projects.
limitations: Quality, compatibility and safety vary by individual upload
Check each creator's page and download details before installing

name: Pomofocus
description: A simple Pomodoro timer for focused work sessions and breaks.
fullDescription: Pomofocus is a browser-based Pomodoro timer that helps structure work into focused intervals separated by breaks. It is useful for study sessions and personal time management; optional paid features may be available.
features: Task list for a work session
limitations: A timer does not guarantee better focus or replace healthy breaks
Some additional features may require payment

name: A Soft Murmur
description: Mix gentle ambient sounds such as rain, wind and waves.
fullDescription: A Soft Murmur provides ambient background sounds that can be mixed to create a personal listening atmosphere for reading, relaxing or focusing.
features: Adjust sound levels to suit a preference
Use as background audio while studying or resting
limitations: It is not a medical or sleep treatment
Requires a browser with audio playback support

name: myNoise
description: Customise ambient sound generators for focus, rest and masking background noise.
fullDescription: myNoise offers interactive sound generators with adjustable sliders, allowing listeners to shape ambient audio such as rain, nature, drones and noise textures. Many generators are available free on the website; donations and optional apps support the project.
features: Wide range of ambient sound generators
Use for focus, relaxation or masking noise
limitations: Some content or app features may be paid or donation-supported
Audio preferences are personal; no guaranteed health benefit

name: Lofi Girl
description: Continuous music livestreams for studying, relaxing and chilling.
fullDescription: Lofi Girl publishes continuous music livestreams, including lo-fi hip-hop, synthwave and jazz-oriented channels. It is an easy way to play background music while studying or taking a break.
features: Different channels for study and chill moods
limitations: Requires an internet connection
Music streams may include platform advertising and are not an offline player

name: YOPmail
description: Create disposable email addresses and check temporary inboxes without registering.
fullDescription: YOPmail provides disposable email inboxes intended to help reduce spam when signing up for websites. Its inboxes are not password-protected and messages are retained for a limited period, so it must not be used for private, sensitive or account-recovery messages.
features: Create an inbox without account registration
Use temporary addresses to reduce exposure of a primary email
Messages are retained for a limited period
limitations: Inbox names are not password-protected and may be guessable
Do not receive banking, personal, confidential or account-recovery messages
Some websites block disposable email domains

name: Have I Been Pwned
description: Check whether an email address appears in known data breaches.
fullDescription: Have I Been Pwned lets people check email addresses against known breach records and review exposed breach information. It also provides breach notifications and other services. A match means the address appeared in a listed breach; it does not by itself prove an account is currently compromised.
features: Check an email address against known breach records
Review breach timelines and exposed data categories
limitations: A result is limited to breaches in the service dataset
A clean result does not guarantee an account has never been exposed
Use the official site and never share passwords

name: FMHY — Free Media Heck Yeah
description: A community-curated directory of free digital resources, tools and websites.
fullDescription: FMHY is a large community-maintained index covering topics such as privacy, AI, streaming, listening, gaming, reading, software, education and miscellaneous internet resources. It is an index of third-party links rather than a host for the listed files. Check the destination, copyright rules and local laws before using linked services.
features: Browse a wide range of curated resource categories
Discover tools, media resources and online services
limitations: Links lead to third-party websites with their own risks and terms
Availability and legality vary by resource and location
Use caution with downloads, advertisements and unofficial mirrors

name: JSLinux
description: Run selected Linux and other operating-system environments directly in your browser.
fullDescription: JSLinux is an in-browser computer emulator by Fabrice Bellard. It offers several emulated systems, including Linux distributions and other legacy environments, allowing users to experiment with operating systems without installing them locally. Performance and available hardware features depend on the emulated system and browser.
features: Run supported emulated operating systems in a browser
Experiment with Linux terminals and selected graphical environments
Try different CPU architectures and system images
limitations: Emulation is slower and more limited than native hardware
Available systems and features are defined by the project
Do not treat an emulated environment as a secure production machine

name: Grabify — Tracking-Link Awareness
description: A privacy-awareness reference about link-based IP logging and tracking risks.
fullDescription: Grabify is associated with IP-logging links that can expose connection metadata when someone opens a crafted URL. This listing is included only to explain the privacy risk and help users recognise tracking links. Do not use tracking links to identify, monitor or target people without their informed consent.
limitations: Can expose visitors’ IP-related and request metadata
Do not use for covert tracking, harassment or identifying people
IP addresses do not reliably reveal a person’s exact identity or home address

name: Call Bomber — Safety Awareness
description: A safety-awareness entry about phone-bombing services and unwanted call or SMS flooding.
fullDescription: Phone-bombing services are associated with repeatedly sending calls or messages to a target number. This entry is listed for awareness, not as an endorsement or instruction to use such services. The reviewed Call Bombers page describes itself as an informational visual simulator and states that it does not place real calls or send SMS. Never use services to harass or disrupt another person.
limitations: Do not use phone-bombing services against real people or numbers
Repeated unwanted calls or messages can constitute harassment
The reviewed page describes its simulator as non-operational; claims may change
